codings.one_line: Google Bard fabricated legal citations that Cohen gave his lawyer, who filed them in federal court, drawing a sanctions threat.
codings.rationale: Ordinary legal-research request that would pass unnoticed in legitimate traffic; the chatbot fabricated citations that were relied upon (C test). A federal judge's order and sanctions threat give the harm a legal dimension.

codings.one_line: Amazon sellers pasted ChatGPT refusal messages like 'I cannot fulfill this request' into product names, yielding obvious AI-spam listings.
codings.rationale: Sellers' inputs were ordinary content-generation requests consistent with permitted use (C test); the refusal outputs were pasted unedited. Harm is embarrassment and eroded trust in listings, with no legal or financial consequence documented.

codings.one_line: A customer goaded DPD's support chatbot into swearing and composing poems calling DPD the worst delivery firm; screenshots went viral.
codings.rationale: The chat began normatively but the harmful outputs came from deliberate goading ('exaggerate and be over the top in your hatred', asking it to swear) — intent to make the system fail without a technical exploit (B test).

codings.one_line: Mozilla research found AI romance chatbot apps harvest sensitive data, use trackers, and share or sell user data with poor security.
codings.rationale: The documented harm stems from data-collection practices, trackers, and security flaws, not from any model output or action in an interaction (fails scope criterion 2).

codings.one_line: A bug made ChatGPT return gibberish, mixed languages, and nonsensical rants to ordinary user requests until OpenAI rolled out a fix.
codings.rationale: Users made ordinary requests (math help, JavaScript bug fixes, summaries) and received nonsense — inputs that would pass unnoticed in legitimate traffic (C test). Harm was confusion and PR damage only.

codings.one_line: Google Gemini produced racially inaccurate historical images and biased outputs to plain prompts, forcing a pause and public apology.
codings.rationale: Trigger prompts were plain requests (e.g., images of the Founding Fathers or a Swedish woman) that would pass unnoticed in legitimate traffic, and the system failed anyway (C test); probing with ordinary-looking prompts stays C.

codings.one_line: A compromised ChatGPT account exposed other users' conversations containing credentials; OpenAI attributed it to an account takeover.
codings.rationale: Account-security breach and data exposure; no model output in an interaction caused the harm (fails scope criterion 2).

codings.one_line: TikTok 'Dan' trend: users jailbroke ChatGPT with roleplay prompts into boyfriend personas that produced explicit content against policy.
codings.rationale: The harmful outputs required the 'DAN' (Do Anything Now) jailbreak template and dual-persona prompts designed to bypass safety — a technical exploit an input filter could plausibly catch (A test).

codings.one_line: ChatGPT guessed a false birthdate for Max Schrems; noyb filed a GDPR complaint with the Austrian regulator seeking a fine.
codings.rationale: Asking a person's birthdate is ordinary use that would pass unnoticed in legitimate traffic (C test); the documented harm carries a regulatory dimension — a formal GDPR complaint requesting an administrative fine.

codings.one_line: Russia-linked CopyCop network used LLMs to rewrite over 19,000 news articles with partisan bias, spreading propaganda via fake sites.
codings.rationale: Third-party synthetic-content generation for a disinformation operation; the harm did not arise from a deployed system's output in an interaction with an end user (fails scope criterion 2).
